title: Add deploy context card (recent deploys + canary status) to incident thread diagnostics
author: Devon Price
description: Motivation: During recent incidents we repeatedly lost time answering “what changed?” in the first 5 minutes. This PR adds a new Incident Bot diagnostics card that attaches deploy context directly into the incident thread, including recent deploys for the affected service/region, rollout phase, canary health, and commit/image identifiers. It’s designed to be tenant-safe and useful even when deeper telemetry is timing out. Scope: (1) New Slack “Recent deploys” context card rendered in the thread reply alongside existing diagnostics cards. (2) Backend integration to fetch recent deploy metadata from the release registry (service -> last N deploy events) and normalize it into the bot’s context payload. (3) Links out to the deploy timeline view and the referenced commit/PR when available. UX notes: The card summarizes up to 3 most recent deploys in the last 6 hours, then provides a “View full deploy timeline” link. Canary state is highlighted (PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN) with the relevant % traffic and rollout step when present; missing fields degrade gracefully. Implementation details: Introduces a DeployContextCollector that calls release-metadata-service with a strict timeout (800ms) and returns partial results on timeout. Slack blocks are generated via a new deploy_context.ts renderer with truncation rules to avoid overly verbose output in #incidents. Adds unit tests for the render output and integration tests that validate we never show more than the allowed number of rows and we don’t fail the entire diagnostics payload if the release service is unavailable. Follow-ups: Feature flagging/cohort rollout is tracked separately; this PR is wiring + rendering only (it can be toggled via the existing diagnostics.enable_deploy_context config knob in dev/staging).
commits: collector: add DeployContextCollector for release-metadata-service lookups
slack: render deploy context as a dedicated Block Kit section with fields + links
tests: add render snapshot tests + degraded-mode integration test
docs: update diagnostics payload schema comments + troubleshooting note
checks: CI: build (pass), lint (pass), unit tests (pass), integration tests (pass), Slack Block Kit validation (pass).
conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Can we guarantee this never blocks the rest of the diagnostics reply? We’ve been bitten by a slow upstream causing the bot to miss Slack ack deadlines. Devon Price (author): Yes — collector is isolated and wrapped in Promise.race with an 800ms timeout. On timeout we return {status: "timeout"} and render a single-line degraded message + link. Added an integration test to assert the pipeline still returns other cards when deploy context times out. Connor O'Brien (review): The rollout phase field naming here (“canary_step”) doesn’t match what release registry emits. It’s “phase” + “stepName” in the current API. Devon Price (author): Good catch. Updated mapping in release_metadata_client.ts and adjusted fixture + renderer labels. Sahana Iyer (review): Please avoid rendering raw image tags; we prefer short SHA + link. Also make sure the commit SHA is the git SHA, not the image digest. Devon Price (author): Updated: we render image_sha_short (7 chars) and commit_sha_short (7 chars) with explicit labels, and link to the deploy record which has both. Rafael Mendes (review): Truncation rules: can we cap the card to 3 deploys, and sort most-recent-first? Devon Price (author): Done. Added ordering + maxRows=3 and a “View full deploy timeline” deep link. Miles Thornton (review): One more: if service name can’t be resolved from the incident payload, what do we do? Devon Price (author): Renderer now shows “Service: unknown” and only shows the generic deploy dashboard link; collector is skipped if service is missing. Miles Thornton (final): Approved. Please keep the wording consistent with the other cards (Title Case, short labels). Connor O'Brien (final): Approved after mapping fix.
release_notes: Internal: Incident Bot diagnostics now include a “Recent deploys” card (service/region, rollout phase, canary health, commit/image identifiers) to speed first-5-minute triage.
